procedural_history.originating_court: High Court of Delhi at New Delhi
procedural_history.impugned_order: Judgment and order dated 01.07.2024 passed by the learned Single Judge of the High Court of Delhi at New Delhi in Bail Application Nos.1675 and 1739 of 2024.
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: The learned Single Judge of the High Court of Delhi at New Delhi refused to grant bail to the appellant in Bail Application Nos. 1675 and 1739 of 2024.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The appellants challenged the High Court's order refusing bail in the Supreme Court. The Supreme Court allowed the appeals, quashing and setting aside the High Court's judgment and order.

directions: The impugned judgment and order dated 01.07.2024 passed by the learned Single Judge of the High Court of Delhi at New Delhi in Bail Application Nos.1675 and 1739 of 2024 are quashed and set aside;

issue.issue_text: Whether the custody of the appellant is necessary for the purpose of investigation when the charge-sheet and complaint have already been filed.

facts: The Supreme Court noted that in the case investigated by the CBI, a charge-sheet had already been filed.
The Court also observed that in the case investigated by the ED, a complaint had been filed.
application: The appellant's counsel argued that since the investigation was complete, as evidenced by the filing of the charge-sheet and complaint, the appellant's further custody was not required.
The Court agreed with this premise, stating that the filing of these documents meant that the investigation phase was over.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court concluded that because the charge-sheet and complaint had been filed, the appellant's custody was not necessary for the purpose of investigation.

arguments.issue_text: Whether the custody of the appellant is necessary for the purpose of investigation when the charge-sheet and complaint have already been filed.
appellant_arguments: Since the complaint and the charge-sheet have already been filed, the investigation is complete.
As the investigation is complete, the further custody of the appellant is not required.
There is no material on record to implicate the appellant with the offences they are charged with.
respondent_arguments: The provided text does not contain the respondent's specific arguments on this issue. The respondent's counsel (ASG) suggested that the Court should avoid elaborate discussions on the merits of the case to prevent prejudicing the rights of either party at trial.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: The fundamental right of liberty provided under Article 21 of the Constitution is superior to statutory restrictions, and the principle that 'bail is the rule and refusal is an exception' must be upheld.
obiter: Courts, while deciding such matters, should exercise their discretion judiciously using their prudence.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: On perusal of the record, the Court found that in the CBI case a charge-sheet has been filed and in the ED case a complaint has been filed. As such, the custody of the appellant is not necessary for the purpose of investigation.
legal_tests_applied: Bail is the rule and refusal is an exception.
The fundamental right of liberty provided under Article 21 of the Constitution is superior to the statutory restrictions.
policy_considerations: Prolonged incarceration before being pronounced guilty of an offence should not be permitted to become punishment without trial.
